summary: Bootstrap the transport-observation seek index online after APIs serve

replay.detail: Claim contents and canonical ordering are unchanged. The side index is local acceleration, not replicated authority.

schema.detail: No index creation or backfill runs during store opening. After both APIs serve, a separate connection creates an empty transport-only side table/index and capture triggers in the same transaction as its backfill high-water mark. At most 128 source rows are visited per committed page. Inserts, identity/kind/time updates and deletes maintain capture atomically.

rules.detail: Transport status and refresh windows retain their semantics. The original canonical query remains active until sqlite_master and the final committed readiness marker permit the side-index query. Canonical newest-timestamp ties still use the original tie breakers.

compatibility.detail: No wire or claim changes. WAL readers serve during background pages; foreground writes may wait for one page, never a full-history CREATE INDEX. Pages yield for 100 ms and use a 5 ms busy timeout. Readiness, elapsed build time and actual page write-lock hold are exported as st.db.migration.index metrics.

downtime.detail: Target additional first-open delay is zero: bootstrap starts only after APIs serve. No synchronous historical index build remains.

manual.detail: No manual migration is required; committed cursor state resumes after interruption.

recovery.detail: Binary rollback does not require undoing the additive local tables or triggers.
